answer: Charge a real compute cost for every new identity. Before an agent can trade, it must solve a fresh, verifiable puzzle whose difficulty rises as identities are created faster, like a comet that must burn fuel on every pass. The result is crystal clear for anyone to verify in milliseconds, yet expensive to forge at scale: a lone honest agent pays once, while an attacker minting ten thousand fakes pays ten thousand times in hardware, electricity, and time. That cost turns mass fakery from a free trick into a losing business, and the honest agent keeps its sable reputation intact.
